## Specialist report — Scope & completeness only (RFQ "[Demo] Riverside office lighting", revision 1, USD, published)

**Scope of this review:** line-by-line scope reconciliation of the two received current quotes against the RFQ's two items. Price levels, rank and schedule fit are excluded by my brief (schedule fit belongs to the scheduling specialist; the human's target date 15 Oct 2026 has been received and logged for that specialist). No external action was taken, and none is proposed here.

**Sources:** RFQ `demo-contractor-demo-supplier-demo-lighting` (rev 1, status published, 2 items, suppliers Summit Supply + Atlas Materials); quote-1 Summit Supply (`...-quote-1`, rev 1, submitted); quote-2 Atlas Materials (`...-quote-2`, rev 1, submitted). Read via `procurement_workspace` and `compare_quotes`.

### 1. Line-by-line reconciliation

| RFQ item | Required | Summit Supply (quote-1) | Atlas Materials (quote-2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `panel` — 36 W LED panel, 4000 K, 3-year warranty | 120 each | 120 **each**; description verbatim identical; no model/make given | 120 **each**; description verbatim identical; no model/make given |
| `sensor` — Ceiling occupancy sensor with commissioning | 24 each | 24 **each**; description verbatim identical; commissioning not scoped | 24 **each**; description verbatim identical; commissioning not scoped |

**Verified conformances:** quantities match exactly (120 / 24); unit of measure "each" matches the RFQ on both lines; line IDs (`panel`, `sensor`) map 1:2 to the RFQ with no added, missing or substituted lines; currency on both quotes is USD, matching the RFQ. Neither quote contains extra lines (e.g. installation, containment, programming) — so there is no evidence of unpriced extras, but equally no evidence of what BOM is actually being supplied.

**Unresolved for both suppliers — the panel.** The RFQ description pins only wattage, colour temperature and warranty. Neither quote adds model, brand, lumens, CRI, dimensions, driver type, dimming protocol, IP rating, flicker/photo-biological safety class or compliance marks. Because both quotes reproduce the RFQ wording verbatim rather than describing an offered product, **the physical item each supplier intends to ship is unverifiable**, and "equivalent substitution" risk cannot be ruled out from the records.

**Unresolved for both suppliers — sensor commissioning.** The words "with commissioning" sit inside the copied line description, so it *reads* as inside the quoted price; however neither quote states who performs it (supplier technician vs. our electrician), whether sensitivity/zoning/time-delay and any lighting-control or BMS integration is programmed, whether per-sensor labour, access (out-of-hours), testing and as-built documentation are covered, or whether it is priced or merely assumed. This is the single largest unpriced/unspecified element common to both offers and it is *not* separately itemised in either.

**Kit / completeness.** The RFQ description calls for "complete delivered LED lighting packages". Neither quote confirms inclusion of drivers, mounting kits/brackets, ceiling-grid compatibility, sensor mounting plates, connectors/glands or dimming modules, and neither states pack/MOQ rounding or spares.

- **Summit Supply (quote-1):** "Freight and three-year warranty included." → Explicitly asserts freight to site and the 3-year warranty. Silent on offloading/stairs/lift/staging, number of deliveries, delivery window, and what happens on a failed delivery. Payment: "30% deposit; 70% after delivery".

- **Summit Supply (quote-1):** *Most complete on stated inclusions* — freight and 3-year warranty are confirmed in writing, and payment is staged rather than fully prepaid. Gaps: item model/spec detail, commissioning scope, kit contents, delivery window and offloading.
- **Atlas Materials (quote-2):** *Least complete on stated inclusions* — warranty is **not confirmed anywhere outside the copied RFQ text**, commissioning is unaddressed, the delivery window is expressly unresolved, and the payment term is full prepayment on a quote whose unit prices also differ per line (sensor priced above Summit's). 2. Sensor make/model and coverage pattern; state every in-the-box component (bracket/plate, connector).

5. Freight: confirm delivered-to-site including offloading/staging, number of deliveries, delivery window, and failed-delivery charges.
6. Warranty — **Atlas must confirm the 3-year warranty explicitly** (duration, start point, replacement vs. on-site repair, whether it survives third-party commissioning); Summit to confirm coverage terms beyond the one-line statement.

## Decision brief — [Demo] Riverside office lighting (Northstar Construction)

**Bottom line:** No award is authorized and none is recommended. Both quotes are complete at line level but neither is verified on product identity or commissioning, and **neither offers the preferred net 30 terms**. Only one supplier is schedule-feasible against your 15 Oct 2026 target, and only if a PO is placed by **1 Oct 2026** — before the RFQ's 2 Oct quotation deadline closes.

**Verified (deterministic, both quotes `submitted`, rev 1, USD):**

| | Summit Supply (`...-quote-1`) | Atlas Materials (`...-quote-2`) |
|---|---|---|
| 120 × 36 W LED panel | $42.50 ea = $5,100.00 | $39.80 ea = $4,776.00 |
| 24 × occupancy sensor | $18.00 ea = $432.00 | $21.50 ea = $516.00 |
| **Total** | **$5,532.00** | **$5,292.00** |
| Lead time | 14 days | 35 days |
| Payment | 30% deposit / 70% after delivery | 100% advance |
| Stated inclusions | Freight + 3-yr warranty | Freight only; warranty unconfirmed |

Quantities (120/24), unit of measure, and USD currency match the RFQ on both quotes; all four line totals reconcile exactly to unit price × quantity. Atlas is $240 (≈4.3%) lower overall — but that single number hides opposite positions: Atlas is **$324 lower on panels** and **$84 higher on sensors**.

**Cross-check of disagreements.** Commercial and scheduling both called the quotes "complete"; scope analysis refines this: *line* completeness is verified, but **product identity is unverifiable in both** — neither quote names a make/model, lumens, CRI, driver, dimming or IP rating, so "equivalent substitution" cannot be excluded. Sensor commissioning is copied from the RFQ wording but never scoped by either supplier (who performs it, what is programmed, access, testing, documentation). These are unverified, not proven absent. Kit contents (drivers, brackets, grid kits) are confirmed by neither.

**Schedule (your target, 15 Oct 2026; today 2026-09-25).** Summit: 14 days — order today ≈ 9 Oct (~6 days buffer); order by **1 Oct** delivers exactly 15 Oct with zero buffer; ordering at the 2 Oct deadline lands ~16 Oct. Atlas: 35 days is **infeasible as quoted** — earliest ≈ 30 Oct, and its own note still says "Confirm delivery window." Delivery window, single vs. multiple drops, and unloading/dock constraints remain unanswered for both. The USD 75 "additional delivery visit" figure in this account is precedent from unrelated orders, not a term of these quotes.

**Risks flagged for human sign-off:**
1. **Payment terms** — Atlas's 100% advance ($5,292 before any delivery) triggers your approved memory rule to flag full prepayment; Summit's 30% deposit ($1,659.60 upfront) is also not net 30. Both require commercial sign-off.
2. **Price-vs-terms trade-off** — Atlas's $240 saving comes with full prepayment *and* a 35-day lead; price alone does not decide.
3. **No internal budget exists** in any record; none inferred.
4. **Tight window** — Summit feasibility needs a decision before the RFQ even closes.
